chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, from his father, from his grandfather, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) disliked eating five parts: the spleen, the penis, the two testicles, the vagina, and the corners of the heart.
ai.seo_question: What are the five parts of sheep that the Prophet disliked eating?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s specific dietary preferences, distinguishing these five parts from general halal meat through the lens of *karahat* (dislike) rather than prohibition. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet’s detailed bodily and dietary etiquettes, often linking physical purity to spiritual refinement.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-33 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashemi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his forefathers that Ali (MGB) said,
“God’s Prophet (MGB) disliked eating five parts of sheep: the spleen; the penis; the balls; the vagina; and the corners of the heart.”
